newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to easier.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to easier.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended steady to easier in moderate trade on Monday on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate slipped slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to easier. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.96/1.91 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.05/2.00 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.53/1.48 percent against 1.62/1.57 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$99.32/99.37 from last Friday's close of S$99.33/99.38 and June 2003 at S$99.89/99.94 versus S$98.90/98.95.
September 2001 was unchanged from last Friday's close of S$99.37/99.42
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent against last Friday's 3-3/16 3-1/16 percent.
